para.text: XYGRAPH offers the use of polar co-ordinates. In polar co-ordinates the position of a certain point is given by the distance to the origin, and an orientation. The latter is the angle between the line connecting the point and the origin, and the conventional positive X-axis. The angle is measured in the conventional direction (counter-clockwise).

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:none;
para.text: There are two graph types that can be constructed in polar co-ordinates, a polar graph and a radar graph. These are strictly quite different, but have nevertheless much in common. In (nearly) all aspects both are treated as normal 2D graphs having an X and a Y parameter.
In 3D plotting more options are available: cylindrical co-ordinates and spherical co-ordinates. These are more or less extensions of the 2D polar co-ordinates.

para.text: uses strict polar co-ordinates, and are in that sense very similar to normal X-Y graphs. All normal plotting procedures can be used, X represents the radial co-ordinate and Y the angle in degrees (see common features below).

para.text: is a polar graph with an extra vertical angle added to that. The two angles look very much like the longitude and latitude on the world globe. Normal 3D plotting procedures can be used: X represents radial co-ordinate, Y the horizontal angle in degrees (longitude, 0-360) and Z the vertical angle in degrees (latitude, -90 - 90) see also comments below. Plotting here is restricted to lines, symbols, polygons and circles (the latter in a limited way).

The spherical co-ordinates are strictly wrong, customary the second co-ordinate is the vertical angle and is measured from the vertical line downwards (0° pointing upwards). The co-ordinates used here are consistent with the cylindrical co-ordinates and follow the common instinct. However it is possible to set correct spherical co-ordinates in

para.text: - The Y co-ordinate represents an angle in the horizontal plane, when viewed from above 0° points to the right and the positive direction is counter-clockwise. This (mathematical) correct definition differs from the more practical angle in the definition of the viewing position. If A is the angle of the viewing position in degrees, its orientation in cylindrical co-ordinates is 270-A (90+A in reverse mode). This is the angle that is ‘in front’ of the picture.
